objectives.title: Strategic alignment
objectives.statement: Link every agent initiative to a strategic objective before money is spent on it, so that effort does not go to work the organization does not want.
objectives.risk: Agents that do not serve the organization's objectives
objectives.metric: Share of agent initiatives linked to a strategic objective
tiers: The request names the question the experiment is meant to answer.
The request names the business objective and the person who stands behind it.
The portfolio board approves the link to a funded initiative before design starts.
The executive sponsor approves the initiative as part of the strategy.
objectives.evidence: The approved intake record, with the objective, the sponsor and the approval date.

objectives.title: Portfolio rationalization
objectives.statement: Find agents that do the same job, and consolidate them, so that the organization does not pay to build and run the same capability twice.
tiers: The requester searches the catalog before starting an experiment.
Intake checks the catalog for an existing agent that does the job, and records the result.
An architect confirms there is no overlap, or approves the overlap with a reason.
The portfolio is reviewed for overlap each quarter across the whole organization.
objectives.evidence: The catalog search recorded at intake, and the portfolio review with its consolidation decisions.

objectives.title: Standard demand intake
objectives.statement: Send every request for a new agent through one intake process, so that each is evaluated before work begins.
objectives.risk: Uncontrolled growth in the number of agents
objectives.metric: Share of agents that came through intake
tiers: A short self-service form registers the experiment.
The full intake form is completed and triaged within a set time.
Intake includes a first risk tier and an initial list of the obligations from section I.
Intake goes to the portfolio board with a business case.
objectives.evidence: The intake record for the agent, linked from its catalog entry.

objectives.title: Investment governance
objectives.statement: Evaluate what each agent initiative is expected to return before funding it, and compare the result with the projection afterwards.
objectives.risk: Poor use of money on agent initiatives
objectives.metric: Projected return compared with actual return
tiers: Experiments run within a fixed budget set by the team.
The request states the expected cost and benefit.
Finance reviews the business case, and the actual return is compared with it after six months.
The investment committee approves the case, and the comparison is reported to the executive sponsor.
objectives.evidence: The business case, the approval, and the later comparison of projected and actual return.

objectives.title: Dependency mapping
objectives.statement: Record what each planned agent will depend on and what will depend on it, including other agents, so that failures and changes can be traced. The Network discipline governs these relationships once they exist.
objectives.metric: Share of agents with recorded dependencies
tiers: The owner lists the systems the experiment calls.
Every dependency on another agent or system is recorded in the catalog before release.
Dependencies are declared in the agent's signed description and checked against what it actually calls.
The dependency map is reviewed by the owners of every agent on it before release.
objectives.evidence: The declared dependencies in the catalog, and the result of comparing them with observed calls.

objectives.title: A complete agent catalog
objectives.statement: Keep a registry of every agent the organization runs or relies on, with its owner, its tier and its status, so that no agent operates outside governance.
objectives.risk: Agents that governance does not know about
objectives.metric: Share of running agents found in the catalog
tiers: Experiments are registered, and are marked as sandbox only.
Every production agent has a catalog entry with a named owner before it runs.
The catalog entry is the source the run-time checks read, so an unregistered agent cannot run.
The catalog is reconciled with what is actually running each month, and the result is reported.
objectives.evidence: The catalog, and the latest reconciliation between catalog entries and running agents.

objectives.title: Retirement planning
objectives.statement: Set the conditions under which an agent will be retired when it is first approved, so that old agents do not pile up.
objectives.metric: Share of agents with written retirement conditions
tiers: The experiment has an end date.
The agent states the conditions that would end it.
The retirement conditions are checked at every review date.
The retirement plan names who is affected and how they will be told.
objectives.evidence: The retirement conditions in the agent's record, and the review records that checked them.

objectives.title: Strategic risk assessment
objectives.statement: Assess the risks in the agent strategy itself, including dependence on one supplier, technology going out of date and whether the organization is ready.
objectives.risk: Unrecognized risks in the agent strategy
objectives.metric: Share of initiatives with a completed risk assessment
tiers: No separate assessment is needed for an experiment.
The request notes any single supplier the agent would depend on.
Risk reviews the initiative and records how each strategic risk will be handled.
The assessment goes to the executive sponsor and is repeated each year.
objectives.evidence: The risk assessment, the decisions on each risk and who made them.
